references.text: The direct fulfillment of Abraham's prophetic words: God provides a ram as a burnt offering in place of Isaac, and the place is called 'The Lord will provide' (JHVH jir'eh).
John the Baptist points to Jesus as 'the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world' – the ultimate fulfillment that God Himself provides the sacrificial lamb.
Isaiah prophesies about the Lord's suffering servant as a lamb led to slaughter – a typological parallel to the sacrificial lamb that God provides.
Hebrews describes Abraham's faith when he was tested: he believed that God could raise someone from the dead, and received Isaac back as a foreshadowing.
Christ as a spotless Lamb, foreordained before the foundation of the world – God's ultimate provision of the sacrificial lamb, paralleling Genesis 22:8.
Christ gave Himself for us as a gift and a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma to God, echoing God's provision of the burnt offering.
Noah builds an altar and offers burnt offerings to the Lord – an early parallel to the theme of burnt offerings in Abraham's test.
Both verses are part of the same continuous event (Abraham's test) and show the connection between God's call and Abraham's faithful response.
John 8:56 reveals the messianic insight behind Abraham's faithful response in Genesis 22:8.
Hebrews 11:17 reveals the belief in resurrection that underpinned Abraham's response in Genesis 22:8.
